execution: decide at close, fill at next open, long-only, no leverage
hypothesis: Crypto trends persist for hours to days because flows are herd-like and the market never closes. A fast hourly EMA above a slow one captures that drift, but it fails in two regimes: calm chop (no trend to ride, costs eat the signal) and panic spikes (gaps and reversals). Trading only when one-week realized volatility sits in the middle band of its own trailing 90-day distribution should keep the trend edge and skip the regimes where it historically breaks.
rules: Every hourly bar close, per asset: fast EMA (24 bars) above slow EMA (96 bars) means an up-trend.
Realized volatility = standard deviation of hourly log returns over the last 168 bars (one week).
Regime filter: volatility must lie between its trailing 25th and 75th percentile over the last 2160 bars (90 days); calm chop and panic spikes are skipped.
Hold the asset (weight 1/3 of capital per asset, unused slots stay in cash) while up-trend AND middle-band volatility are both true; otherwise flat.
Decide at the bar close, fill at the next bar open, long-only, no leverage. Periods are hourly bars (24/7), not days.
